findings.comment: matches gates/G2.json seed_mean_unweighted at both resolutions

gates/G2.json reports seeds_with_positive_advantage = 0 without naming a weighting, and the decision document says 'negative in 3/3 seeds at both resolutions'. Person-weighted, seed 0 is POSITIVE at both resolutions (+0.00216 at 64, +0.00007 at 256). Seed means stay negative under both weightings, so the G2 verdict is unaffected.
|estimate|/SE = 0.16, 0.98, 0.41 at |T|=64: within ~1 SE of zero, i.e. no demonstrated advantage and no demonstrated deficit, as the decision document itself states.
|estimate|/SE = 0.72, 3.07, 2.64 at |T|=256, where the probe carries 276 input columns against the baseline's 20 on 2048 fitting rows; a width handicap is a live explanation of the deficit.

findings.item: size of the 'subsumption' difference against its own uncertainty
findings.comment: the difference that motivates the word 'subsumed' is 0.16-0.98 SE. It supports 'no measurable improvement at this probe capacity', not an information-theoretic subsumption claim.

findings.item: B1 decile partition is built from per-row loss, which reads the residence label
findings.comment: stage_b.run_seed: decile_cells = digitize(_baseline_score(ref_j, j_val), ...); _baseline_score returns probe['per_row_loss']; _per_row computes -log p[i, y_i] from y_val = the residence label. The partition coordinate is therefore a function of each person's own label.

ten cells reduce residence log loss from ~0.52 to 0.065-0.094 nats. No label-free 10-cell partition of a service-probability view can do that; the fixture b1_label_leak_fixture.py reproduces the effect on a label that is pure noise.
